description:
Supplementary software and data for the article Identifiability of species interactions in a living material: Bayesian calibration of an extended Hamilton principle multiphase model (submitted to Extreme Mechanics Letters).

The archive contains (i) the JAX implementation of the five-species extended-Hamilton-principle biofilm model and of the GPU-accelerated transitional Markov chain Monte Carlo (TMCMC) sampler used to infer the 15 entries of the symmetric interaction matrix, (ii) the job script that defines the four inference stages (i) pilot, (ii) p1, (iii) p2, (iv) ult, (iii) the posterior samples, log-likelihoods, MAP estimates and full run records (configuration, prior boxes, tempering history, convergence diagnostics) of every run shown in the paper, three seeds per stage and condition, (iv) the final MAP estimates and initial conditions, and (v) the scripts that regenerate the figures, tables and checks of the paper and its supplementary material, together with the outputs used in the manuscript.

The experimental time courses (species fractions, biofilm volume, membrane integrity, pH) used for calibration are not included in this archive; they are those of Heine et al. (2025), Front. Oral Health 6:1649419, https://doi.org/10.3389/froh.2025.1649419, and must be cited as such.

See README.md for the directory layout, software versions and the command lines that reproduce each figure and table.
notes: Related dataset: the experimental data are from Heine et al. (2025), Influence of species composition and cultivation condition on peri-implant biofilm dysbiosis in vitro, Frontiers in Oral Health 6:1649419, doi:10.3389/froh.2025.1649419. Inference runs were performed on a single NVIDIA GPU per run with JAX in double precision (jax_enable_x64).
